### Astro Quest – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Astro Quest is an interactive, kid-friendly web-based space exploration platform designed for children aged 7–12. It transforms space learning into an exciting astronaut adventure where young learners can experience simulated space missions and make important decisions.

The platform allows children to take on the role of junior astronauts and complete mission challenges by managing essential resources such as oxygen, power, and fuel. Through interactive scenarios and decision-making activities, children learn how astronauts plan missions, manage limited resources, and overcome challenges in space.

Astro Quest addresses the challenge by providing an engaging and accessible way for children to understand the complexities of space missions through hands-on virtual experiences. Instead of simply reading about space, children actively participate, experiment, and learn from their decisions.

The project is important because it encourages curiosity about space science, develops critical thinking and problem-solving skills, and makes STEM education more interactive, enjoyable, and accessible to young learners.
details:
Project Details – Astro Quest: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Astro Quest is an interactive, web-based space exploration and astronaut training platform designed for children aged 7–12. It transforms space science into an exciting learning adventure where children become junior astronauts and explore different space missions.

The platform offers four interactive training sectors: Rocket Builder Lab, Solar System Safari, Alien Signal Decoder, and Zero-G Spacewalk Simulator. Children can explore planets through the Planet Hopper Quiz, test their knowledge through interactive questions, earn astronaut achievement badges, and interact with ASTRO, an AI-powered virtual astronaut co-pilot that answers space-related questions.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

Astro Quest makes complex space science concepts easier and more enjoyable for young learners. It encourages curiosity about the universe while developing logical thinking, problem-solving abilities, creativity, and interest in STEM education. Our intended impact is to inspire children to explore science and develop an interest in future space exploration.

Tools and Technologies:

We used AI-assisted development tools, including Google Antigravity, to support website design and development. The project was developed using web technologies, including HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with GitHub for project management and version control and Vercel for deployment and public access.

Creativity and Team Considerations:

The creative aspect of Astro Quest is its combination of space exploration, interactive simulations, gamification, quizzes, and AI assistance in one child-friendly platform. Our team considered the target age group, ease of navigation, engaging visuals, educational value, accessibility, and age-appropriate content while developing the project. We aimed to make learning feel like playing an astronaut training game rather than attending a traditional lesson.
